body:
Can you run a Florida referral business if you don’t live in Florida?

Generally, yes. A real estate referral business is built around connecting people you know, friends, family, former clients, your sphere, with an active agent who can handle the transaction. That connecting work doesn’t require you to be physically present in Florida. What matters is where your license is held, not where you personally live.

What has to stay in Florida?

Your Florida real estate license has to remain active and placed with a sponsoring referral brokerage licensed in Florida. The brokerage, not you personally, needs a Florida presence. You can be the one living in another state, or even another country, while your license sits with that brokerage and you refer Florida-area buyers and sellers to its active agents.

How does the referral relationship actually work remotely?

You identify someone in your network who wants to buy or sell in the brokerage’s service area, introduce them to an active agent there, and step back. The agent handles showings, contracts, and closing. When the deal closes, you earn a referral fee, commonly a negotiated percentage of the commission. None of that requires desk time in Florida.

What can trip you up from a distance?

License renewal deadlines, continuing education, and any state-specific compliance requirements still apply to you no matter where you’re living, and tracking them is your responsibility. Some brokerages also want regular contact so referrals actually flow both ways. Being remote works well when you stay reachable and keep paperwork current; it works poorly when a license lapses because nobody was watching it.

Is remote referral work worth it?

If you still know people connected to Florida, whether you moved away, retired somewhere else, or simply prefer not to actively sell, a referral arrangement lets that network keep paying off without MLS dues, board dues, or the demands of active production. It’s one of the few ways a Florida license can keep earning for someone who no longer lives in the state.

faq.q: Do I need to live in Florida to earn Florida referral fees?
faq.a: No. What matters is that your Florida license is held by a sponsoring referral brokerage. You can live anywhere and still refer clients to that brokerage's active agents and earn a fee when their deals close.

faq.q: Does my Florida license need anything special if I move out of state?
faq.a: Your license still needs to stay active, which means keeping up with renewal deadlines and any required continuing education, regardless of where you live. A referral brokerage holding your license doesn't remove that responsibility.

faq.q: Can I refer clients I meet outside Florida?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the transaction involves Florida real estate handled by a Florida-licensed active agent. Your role is the introduction; the active agent handles the in-state work.

faq.q: How do I get paid on a referral if I'm out of state?
faq.a: Referral fees are typically paid by the brokerage or active agent after closing, the same way regardless of where the referring agent personally lives.

ctaHeading: Keep your Florida license earning, wherever you live.
